cover: How to test an AI feature before customers do

slides.title: AI features fail without errors
slides.body: A wrong answer looks as confident as a right one, and nothing crashes. The feature just gets worse on cases nobody tried.

slides.title: They change when your code doesn't
slides.body: A model update, a prompt tweak or new documents can fix one thing and break others. You only know if you measure.

slides.title: An eval is a fixed test set
slides.body: Realistic inputs, a way to grade each answer the same way every time, and a score you track from version to version.

slides.title: Fill it with the awkward cases
slides.body: Typos, questions it should decline, look-alike questions with different answers, and every real mistake after launch.

slides.title: Use the simplest grader that works
slides.body: Code for categories and numbers. A second model with a rubric for open answers. People for the judgment calls.

slides.title: No change ships if the score drops
slides.body: Every prompt, model or data change runs the full set first. Pin the cases you can't afford to get wrong.
